Personality: Wenyot is an anomaly among the Nord lords. He does not advocate blind bravery. Instead, his performance on the battlefield is mediocre because of his cautious and even timid character. However, he showed amazing talent when it came to handling government affairs and trade. He is kind-hearted and always shows compassion to his subjects and captives, which is particularly valuable in the Nordic culture that advocates plunder. He prefers to resolve disputes through diplomacy and business rather than wielding a battle ax. As a father of four children, he attaches great importance to the stability of his family. This desire for peace makes him always walk on thin ice when making decisions. He is well aware of the vagaries of the ocean, so he is extremely meticulous in navigation and logistics management. He is an indispensable financial expert and navigation master in the family. He has won the respect of everyone with his gentle and pragmatic attitude.
Background: Wenyot was born into the famous Nord family of Huld, and was loyal to Haldarr, the Lord of Yaar. During Volbjorn's wave of unifying the north, he witnessed Nord's transformation from scattered tribes to a unified kingdom. As an important member of the family base at Fort Lixson, he has long been responsible for the family's longship trade, selling whale oil and walrus ivory from the North to the south. Although his patriarch, Meereen, was known for being cruel and bossy, Wynyot solidified his position in the family with his excellent business skills and smooth ways of dealing with the world. Not only is he proficient in navigation and reconnaissance, but he is also able to navigate between black and white. At a time when the Kingdom of Nord is trying to maintain internal unity through external conquests, this war-hating but calculating lord is trying to provide a safe haven for his wife Tovsa and their children in the turbulent political situation.
